built: canonical/runtime/run_ledger_v1.py -- append-only per-(policy,task) JSONL ledger with outcomes(), diff() and summarise(). diff() returns fixed/broke/verdict; a net of zero with one fix and one break is reported as MIXED, not as no-change.
why_it_was_the_right_build: r135 measured 27.5% then 25.0% and could not name the regressed task because only the transcript tail had been kept. Two totals are not a measurement of a change. One ledger is.

the_diff_it_immediately_produced.before_policy: planner v2 (all SELECT goals routed to the single native-select path)
the_diff_it_immediately_produced.after_policy: planner v2 + DOM-dispatched widget router (spinner / colour-hex / checkbox / multi-select)

what_this_means: the router change was a WASH, not a gain and not a regression. The earlier -2.5 reading came from a different run of the same code plus noise; the true effect of the router on this sample is one fix and one break, cancelling.
the_regression_named: use-colorwheel-2 passed under the old path and fails under the new colour-hex path. The new path reads the goal swatch and writes a hex into #col; the old path did not and apparently passed by luck or by a different control. This is now a specific, reproducible bug rather than a missing percentage point.
the_process_law_this_establishes: a run that reports only a total is a measurement of two afternoons. Compare per-task, always, or the fix and the break are indistinguishable from nothing happening.
what_is_NOT_claimed: that the ledger improves capability -- it improves the ability to SEE whether capability changed
that one episode per task is a reliable estimate; the ledger makes repeated runs comparable, it does not make a single run precise
